title: Representation Transitions Reveal Emerging Safety Risks in Multi-Turn LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.00400v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multi-turn attacks on agentic systems can compose individually permissible actions into harmful outcomes, challenging defenses that assess actions or states in isolation. We show that such attacks leave a detectable signature in the agent's internal representations: harmful behavior emerges as an accumulated representation transition across context updates, whose triggering context can be identified from the same signal. We further find that naive aggregation is confounded by benign representation drift, as a contrastive safety direction need not assign zero to benign transitions. We address this by denoising the direction, anchoring benign traffic at zero and removing its leading variation directions, with no runtime cost.   These findings motivate DART, a runtime framework that detects and attributes representation shifts and intervenes with targeted reminders. Across six models and two multi-turn benchmarks, DART reduces attack succ

translated_title: 表征转变揭示多轮LLM智能体中显现的安全风险
translated_abstract: 对智能体系统的多轮攻击可以将单独看来可允许的动作组合成有害结果，这对孤立评估动作或状态的防御机制构成了挑战。我们证明，此类攻击会在智能体的内部表征中留下可检测的特征：有害行为作为跨上下文更新过程中累积的表征转变而显现，且其触发上下文可以从同一信号中识别出来。我们进一步发现，朴素的聚合方式会受到良性表征漂移的干扰，因为对比学习得到的安全方向不一定会将良性转变映射为零。为此，我们通过对该方向进行去噪来解决这一问题，将良性流量锚定在零点并移除其主要变化方向，且不产生任何运行时开销。这些发现催生了DART——一个运行时框架，它能够检测并归因表征漂移，并通过针对性提醒进行干预。在六个模型和两个多轮基准测试上，DART降低了攻击成功率。
tldr: 该论文发现多轮攻击会在LLM智能体内部表征中留下可检测的累积表征转变信号，并提出DART框架，通过去噪安全方向来检测、归因有害的表征漂移并施以针对性提醒干预，从而有效降低攻击成功率。
en_tdlr: The paper shows that multi-turn attacks leave a detectable signature of accumulated representation transitions in LLM agents' internal representations, and proposes DART, a zero-cost runtime framework that denoises a safety direction to detect, attribute, and intervene in harmful representation shifts with targeted reminders, reducing attack success across six models.
